bull.b: Positive Phase 2b data across multiple liver measures strengthen pemvidutide’s clinical foundation and support continued development in MASH. The concurrent antifibrotic findings may broaden its therapeutic relevance and improve the strategic value of the program as Phase 3 execution advances.

A substantial cash position provides funding visibility for the pivotal PERFORMA program and reduces near-term dependence on capital markets. This supports uninterrupted clinical execution through an important data readout and gives management more flexibility to pursue development priorities.

Development across MASH, AUD and ALD creates several potential applications for one asset and expands the company’s strategic opportunity beyond a single indication. Progress across related liver diseases may improve the value of clinical infrastructure, data, and future commercialization capabilities.

bear.b: Altimmune remains a development-stage company without meaningful recurring product revenue, while losses remain deeply negative. This limits internal funding capacity and leaves future operating performance dependent on successful clinical development, regulatory progress, and eventual commercialization.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business is consuming capital rather than generating it. Although burn improved year over year, continued spending on multiple trials means financing needs and cash management remain important constraints on long-term financial flexibility.

The AUD opportunity remains strategically attractive but its next pivotal step is not yet fully defined. Regulatory feedback, trial scope, sizing, and funding must still be resolved, creating execution uncertainty and potentially delaying development or increasing the capital required to advance the program.
